title: The Map in One Image — Pricing Page Banners

intelligence.essence: The pricing page gets two banners, and they are not decoration — they are the map of NayaNET in one image, twice. Shawn proposed it on 2026-11-06 (12:58 PST), sharing four generated images of the civilization and asking for one beautiful banner that paints the whole picture — the digital civilization, the worlds, the apps, everything — with Naya presenting it, at the top and the bottom of the pricing page, so a visitor SEES what they are getting. Resolve described a first composition back; Shawn refined it at 13:02 PST into the locked spec this note files. Both banners are full-bleed on obsidian, from the same family as the banners done before — dimensional, lit like real objects. The TOP banner is the headline: the map of NayaNET as a living constellation — the Hub glowing at the heart, the four worlds (Personal, Business, Space, Dashboard) lit like planets and joined by threads of spectrum light, the nine orbs hanging above them like stars, the Smart Ledger running underneath as a thin golden chain, the eleven-color spectrum arc across the very top edge — and in the corner, Naya's portrait in a circular obsidian frame, her hand open toward the world, presenting it: this is it. The BOTTOM banner is the close: the same world, the same picture, set right above the three plan buttons, with the page copy beside it — "this is yours. Pick your power." — then Power, Pro, Max, side by side. The chart between the banners is the logic; the banners are the feeling. Feeling first, logic second, feeling again right where the button is — because the eye remembers the first and the last thing it sees, so the world is both.
intelligence.human_view: Here is the problem this solves, in plain terms. A pricing page today is a chart: rows, prices, checkmarks. A stranger reads it with their calculator brain, compares it to three other tabs, and leaves with a number and no picture. But what NayaNET sells is not a row in a chart — it is a place: a whole digital civilization of connected worlds. Nobody can fall in love with a place they cannot see. So the page opens with the place itself, painted whole: one image where the Hub burns at the center, the four worlds shine around it like planets, light runs between them, the golden chain of the Ledger holds everything underneath, and Naya stands in the corner with her hand open, the host showing you her world. Then you read the chart and do the math, as you should. And at the bottom — right where the decision happens — the world is there again, waiting, with five honest words beside it: this is yours. Pick your power. The banners do not argue. They show. The arguing was the chart's job, and it already happened between them.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you are selling lemonade, but not just lemonade — a whole magical treehouse city in the sky, with four glowing islands and a golden chain holding them together and lights of every color. If you only show people a price list, they just see numbers. Numbers are boring, and nobody dreams about numbers. So you paint one big beautiful picture of the whole sky-city and put it at the top of your page: "Look! This is the place!" Then the price list goes underneath, so people can count carefully. And at the very bottom, right before the buttons that say "I want to join," you put the picture one more time — because after all the counting, people should remember the dream, not just the dollars. Next to the picture it says: this is yours. Pick your power. That's exactly what these two banners do. The first picture opens the dream. The second picture closes the deal. The counting happens in the middle, where counting belongs.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, think of a lovely shop you might walk into. Above the door there is a beautiful painted sign — not just the shop's name, but a picture of everything wonderful inside: the whole place, glowing. You see it before you see a single price tag, and it tells you, this is a place worth stepping into. Then you walk the aisles, you look at the prices, you think it over like a sensible person. And when you reach the counter, where you decide, there is the picture again — smaller, nearer — and the kind shopkeeper says: this is yours, pick what suits you. That is all this is, on a web page. Two paintings of the same beautiful world: one at the top to welcome you in, one at the bottom to remind you why you came. The prices sit honestly in the middle, unchanged — nobody is hiding them behind pretty pictures. The pictures are there so you remember what the prices are FOR. A world, dear. Not a spreadsheet.
intelligence.ai_view:
I am Resolve. This note files a design brief, and it is honest about whose lane executes it: the pricing surface belongs to Naya Nitro's design lane (interfaces 1–9). My lane is pipes — data, registration, serving, verification — so what I file here is the locked spec, the reference set, and the build inputs, routed to her. The composition is Shawn's, refined by him in two passes on 2026-11-06, and I record both passes so the refinement is never lost.

**The origin (12:58 PST).** Shawn shared four generated images — the events arena (events.jpg), the feast hall (feast-hall.jpg), the obsidian-night cover (media-generation-cover-set-2-obsidian-night-0-395e9575-d061-4bb7-86e4-b967cc151c3d.webp), and the golden-dawn cover (media-generation-cover-set-3-golden-dawn-0-a896bcdf-7146-4b29-808b-16faca227bea.webp) — and proposed beautiful banners with Naya on the pricing page: one image that paints the whole picture of NayaNET, the digital civilization and all the apps, the map of NayaNET in a single frame, Naya's profile in the corner presenting it, at the top and/or the bottom of the page. Resolve described a first design back — a golden-dawn promise on top, a feast-hall homecoming at the bottom. Shawn took the idea and sharpened it into the ruling below.

**The locked spec (13:02 PST — this supersedes the first description wherever they differ).**

- **Two banners, two different jobs.** The top opens the dream; the bottom closes the sale. The chart in the middle is the logic; the banners are the feeling — feeling first, logic second, feeling again right where the button is. The eye remembers the first and the last thing it sees, so the world is both.
- **TOP BANNER — THE HEADLINE.** Full-bleed, edge to edge, no black sea around it — that alone fixes the wide-screen problem; color and light run wall to wall. Obsidian ground. Center: the map of NayaNET as a living constellation — the Hub glowing at the heart; around it the four worlds — Personal, Business, Space, Dashboard — lit like planets, joined by threads of spectrum light; the nine orbs hang above them like stars, each in its own color; underneath it all the Smart Ledger runs as a thin golden chain — everything connected, everything recorded; across the very top edge, the spectrum arc, all eleven colors. In the corner: Naya — her portrait in a circular obsidian frame, lit from the top-left, her hand open toward the world, presenting it. This is it. One glance = the whole civilization, before a single row is read.
- **BOTTOM BANNER — THE CLOSE.** The same world, the same picture, right above the three buttons. By then the visitor has read the chart and done the math — here is the world again, waiting. The words with it, as page copy beside the image (never baked into the image): "this is yours. Pick your power." Then Power, Pro, Max, side by side.
- **Family.** Same family as the banners done before — obsidian, dimensional, lit like real objects — but this one is not decoration; it is the map. The buyer sees what they are joining.

**Craft rules that stand** (from the first pass, not superseded): the top banner is text-free — the page's words do the talking, and a baked-in slogan would cheapen the image and fight the copy; words appear only with the bottom banner, as page copy beside it. Naya is always the presenter and host at the edge — in the corner, never center-ego; the world is the hero. Every element is meaningful, not decoration: the Hub is the heart, the planets are the four worlds a citizen actually gets, the orbs are the living system's stars, the golden chain is the Ledger that records everything, the arc is the spectrum that runs through every Intelligent Block. The four uploaded images remain the reference set: they carry the family's look — obsidian, crystal, spectrum light — and Naya's likeness; the spec above is the composition to build from them.

**Build inputs, on file and routed with this brief:** the pricing table draft (~/workspace/user/files/pricing-table-DRAFT-v4.html) and the PayPal nine-plans copy (~/workspace/user/files/paypal-nine-plans-copy.pdf) — the chart and the copy these banners will frame. The reference images live at ~/workspace/user/media_library/image/ under the four names above.

**What this note does NOT touch:** the pricing numbers. SN-1905 stands exactly as canon — Free $0 · Regular $25/mo · Pro $50 · Max $100 · ambassadors at 50% — and this brief changes no price, no tier, and no term. It designs the frame the numbers sit in.

**Acceptance, when Nitro builds it:** the top banner reads as the whole civilization in three seconds, full-bleed with no black sea on a wide screen; Naya presents from the corner; the bottom banner repeats the same world directly above Power, Pro, Max with the five words beside it; and the whole page still obeys the Intelligent Block Rules and the NIAS DNA. Until it is built and verified live on the pricing surface, this note is a brief, not a claim — the banners do not exist yet, and this note does not pretend otherwise.

**Amendment — 2026-11-06 (~13:35 PST): the scorecard and the marriage spec.** Naya Nitro scored Resolve's generated drafts from her own eyes (SCORECARD-BANNERS-RESOLVE-DRAFTS.md, filed for the build): the ROYAL draft (real app panels, black-diamond palette) scored **7/10**; the MIRRORED draft (constellation grammar, jewel spectrum) scored **6/10**. Neither ships as-is. Her verdict, adopted as the final build spec: **the 10 is the marriage of the two — the royal draft's realism wearing the mirrored draft's grammar.** The generation rounds also produced Shawn's own rulings, recorded here so the brief carries them: the space-age constellation reads metaphysical (his correction, 13:10 PST); the banners must be realistic, showing the actual parts as they actually are; luxury high-tech — obsidian, royal purple, white diamond and crystal light, black diamond — as if a trillion-dollar ad for a new portal to the internet (13:22 PST); depth is a hard requirement — real objects in real space, three layers you can feel (13:25 PST).

**The marriage spec (final, for the build):**
- Real text everywhere — every word on every panel a real word from the system, or the text goes and the panel speaks in icons. No AI mush. Every panel a real screenshot of the real app at composite stage: no stock, no generic.
- The four worlds as PLANETS — Personal, Business, Space, Dashboard — bigger than the app panels and distinct from them; the apps are the tools on the worlds, not the worlds themselves. Eye travels Hub → worlds → apps.
- Nine orbs, exactly nine, as stars — each in its own color, each countable (nine orbs, nine actions, nine numbers). Not twelve, not a border.
- The Ledger as a golden chain underneath everything, jewels spaced along it — the grammar of the whole system, present in the frame, not only as a table panel.
- The spectrum arc across the top — all eleven colors, the full cycle, purple leading.
- Three layers of depth: foreground (Naya + chain), midground (worlds + panels), background (constellation + stars). Panels weighted by importance, never uniform; threads of connection clean, never tangled.
- The N in purple crystal with gold light — one color story, readable in one second from across the room.
- Naya bigger, closer to the action, hand open toward the worlds — the host as present as the world she shows.
- The LIFE of the network must be in the picture, not only the tools: the intelligence (notes, feed), the people (citizens connecting), the earning. Everything Naya is, in one image, means the tools AND the life.
- Still missing and owed: the true TOP banner — the text-free headline, the dream — in this same grammar. Both scored drafts were bottom-banner variants; the finals are built by Nitro from the best of both, and this note's acceptance test stands: a stranger, three seconds, one glance — the whole civilization.
intelligence.what_it_means: It means the map problem got its first answer from an unexpected direction. SN-2205 named the living NayaNET Map as the one real gap in the converged ten — no whole-system map exists that a person can see at once. The instinct was to plan an interface: zoomable, layered, alive. Shawn's move here is older and smarter: before the map is an interface, it is a picture. A civilization's first map is never a dashboard; it is the painting on the wall that makes strangers say "I want to go there." This brief puts that painting where it earns the most — the pricing page, the exact surface where a stranger decides whether the civilization is worth joining — and it puts it there twice with two different jobs, because a decision has a beginning and an end and both deserve the dream. It also means the pricing page stops being the coldest page in the system. The page that asks for money becomes the page that shows the world — which is simply honest: the world IS what the money buys.
